title: SRE standards: SLOs, error budgets, capacity planning, incident review, operational tooling & runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This page defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, operational tooling, and canonical runbooks. The goal is consistent service-level objectives, a predictable error-budget policy, repeatable capacity planning, and high-quality post-incident reviews across all services that serve customer requests (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane).

Audience
--------
- SRE and Production Engineering
- Service owners (product + platform teams)
- On-call engineers and incident commanders

SLOs & Error Budgets
--------------------
Purpose:
- Make service reliability measurable and actionable.
- Ensure product trade-offs (feature launches, rollouts) are informed by remaining error budget.

SLO template (apply per product route/model):
- Availability (success rate): 99.95% (monthly, rolling 30d)
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 800ms (request end-to-end server-side processing; streaming endpoints measured by final token latency)
- Throttling/Rejects: reject_rate < 0.1% (requests rejected for quota or safety checks)
- Embeddings median latency: < 70ms (per-embedding request)

Primary metrics to compute SLOs (Prometheus naming):
- request_total{route,model} (counter)
- request_success_total{route,model} (counter)
- request_latency_seconds_bucket{le,route,model} (histogram)
- request_rejected_total{reason,route,model} (counter)

Error budget policy (service-level):
1. Compute monthly error budget = 1 - SLO (e.g., for 99.95% SLO, budget = 0.05% of requests).
2. Notification thresholds (rolling 30d):
   - Informational: > 25% budget consumed -> SRE + service owner notified (Slack).
   - Action required: > 50% budget consumed -> freeze non-critical launches; product notified; dedicated triage within 48 hours.
   - Emergency: > 80% budget consumed -> invoke mitigation playbook (scale up, rollback, limit traffic) and declare reliability initiative.
3. If budget exhausted: enforce immediate mitigation steps and require a post-incident review with an action plan before new launches that increase risk.

Capacity planning and forecasting
--------------------------------
Objectives:
- Provision to meet 99th-percentile demand under target latency SLOs with sufficient buffer for failover and bursts.
- Avoid unnecessary overprovisioning while keeping error budget risk low.

Inputs and signals:
- Historical peak RPS (90/95/99 percentiles) by route and model (30/90/180 day windows).
- Avg tokens per request and distribution (prefix-heavy vs. short prompts).
- Model GPU throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) and effective concurrency per instance.
- KV/prefix cache hit ratio and hit latency (reduces GPU work).
- Planned product launches and expected growth rate.

Forecasting formula (simplified):
- Required GPU capacity = ceil((peak_rps * avg_tokens_per_request) / (gpu_tokens_per_sec * effective_concurrency * 3600))
- Add operational buffer: +30% for autoscaling lag and burst tolerance (configurable per service).

Capacity planning cadence and owners:
- Quarterly capacity review (SRE + Infra + product): validate forecasts, adjust reserved/Dedicated commitments.
- Monthly operational check: review top-5 services by growth and GPU utilization.
- Owners: service owners own forecasts; SRE owns validation and scaling runbooks.

Reliability initiatives (RIs)
---------------------------
- RIs are time-boxed projects that address systemic reliability risks (e.g., KV cache regression, routing hot-spots, autoscaler instability).
- Trigger conditions: repeat incidents, recurring SLO breaches, >50% error-budget consumption for 2 consecutive months.
- RI template:
  - Goal (measurable): e.g., reduce p99 latency by 40% on /chat by Dec 1.
  - Metrics: baseline (p50/p95/p99), target, measurement dashboard.
  - Owner: engineering lead + SRE sponsor.
  - Timeline & milestones: discovery, prototype, canary, rollout, validation.
  - Acceptance criteria: objective improvement observed in production and no increased error budget consumption.

Incident review and postmortem standards
---------------------------------------
Severity definitions (apply consistently across teams):
- Sev1: customer-facing outage or severe degradation affecting many customers / causing major revenue or data loss.
- Sev2: partial outage, significant feature degradation, or large performance regressions for subset of customers.
- Sev3: localized failures, non-critical errors, or background job regressions.

Incident lifecycle expectations:
1. Incident page created within 1 hour of detection (incident commander).
2. Initial incident summary published in Slack and status page within 2 hours for Sev1/Sev2.
3. Post-incident review (postmortem) draft published within 72 hours.
4. Final RCA and action items assigned within 7 days.
5. Action items tracked in JIRA and must include owner, ETA, and verification plan; high-priority actions (blocking further launches) are flagged to execs.

Postmortem template (required fields):
- Title, Sev, Incident start/stop timestamps
- Short summary (what happened)
- Impact (customers, functionality, metrics)
- Timeline of events (bullet points with timestamps)
- Root cause analysis (clearly explain contributing factors)
- Detection & mitigation steps (what was done)
- Action items (owner, tracker ticket, ETA)
- Preventative measures & follow-ups (including test or monitoring changes)
- Blameless learning: what we would do differently next time

Operational tooling and dashboards
---------------------------------
Canonical monitoring metrics (per service):
- availability_success_rate{route,model}
- request_latency_seconds{quantiles}
- request_error_rate{route,model}
- gpu_utilization_percent{gpu_pool}
- queue_depth{pool}
- kv_cache_hit_ratio{model}

Standard dashboards (Grafana):
- Service Overview: availability, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, traffic by route
- Capacity: GPU utilization, queue depth, scale events, autoscaler status
- Model Performance: KV cache hit ratio, per-model token throughput

Alerting thresholds (examples, tune per service):
- SLO burn alert: error_budget_burn_rate > 1 (rolling 1h) -> notify SRE + owner
- Error rate: request_error_rate > 0.5% sustained 5m -> PagerDuty (sev2)
- Latency: p95_latency > 800ms 5m -> PagerDuty (sev2)
- GPU saturation: gpu_utilization > 85% for 10m -> warn; > 92% 5m -> PagerDuty (scale)

Tooling stack (recommended):
- Metrics: Prometheus + Cortex
- Dashboards: Grafana (templated panels per service)
- Tracing: Jaeger / OpenTelemetry
- Logging: Loki / ELK for structured request traces
- Incident: PagerDuty (on-call), Slack (incident channel), Statuspage (customer comms)
- Infra automation: Terraform + redwoodctl (internal CLI) + CI pipelines

SRE runbook conventions (format & ownership)
-------------------------------------------
- All runbooks live in Confluence under /eng-sre and include: intent, preconditions, step-by-step recovery, verification steps, and rollback notes.
- Each runbook lists: on-call owner, reviewer, last-tested date, and severity applicability.
- Minimal on-call checklist: link to runbook, runbook owner, escalation path, Slack channel, PagerDuty escalation policy.

Canonical runbooks (examples)
-----------------------------
1) High tail latency (p99) for model serving
- Preconditions: sustained p99 > 1.5x SLO for 10m.
- Steps:
  1. Open service dashboard: confirm p99, queue depth, GPU util, cache hit ratio.
  2. Check KV cache hit ratio: if < expected baseline (e.g., < 60%), consider warming cache via targeted replay job.
  3. Check queue depth: if queue_depth > 50 requests, increase pool using internal CLI:
     - redwoodctl scale --pool <pool-name> --replicas +2
  4. If GPU util > 90% and scale didn't relieve latency within 5m, consider diverting traffic to lower-cost model variant (if available) or apply rate limiting to heavy routes.
  5. After mitigation, verify p99 has returned to within SLO for 15m; document steps in incident page.

2) Error rate spike / 5xx increase
- Preconditions: request_error_rate > 0.5% sustained 5m
- Steps:
  1. Identify error class: check request_rejected_total and request_failure_codes in logs.
  2. If caused by a deployment: roll back the most recent deployment with CI tag (example):
     - redwoodctl rollback --service <svc> --to-tag <previous-tag>
  3. If caused by upstream dependency (e.g., DB/KV availability): fail open to cached responses and notify infra.
  4. Engage engineers for a mitigation patch and create incident page.

3) Autoscaler failures / scale flapping
- Preconditions: repeated scale up/down events causing instability
- Steps:
  1. Inspect autoscaler logs and metrics (scale_events_total, scale_failures_total).
  2. Temporarily fix target capacity to a safe value: redwoodctl scale --pool <pool> --replicas <N> --override-autoscale
  3. Open a ticket for infra to debug autoscaler controller; attach logs and reproduction steps.

Testing and runbook freshness
----------------------------
- Runbooks must be exercised at least once per quarter via on-call game-days.
- After each execution, update the runbook 'last-tested' date and mark any gaps.
- During major launches, runbook owners perform a dry-run with staging traffic.

Governance and enforcement
--------------------------
- SRE Council (monthly): reviews SLO health across top 20 services, approves reliability initiatives, and enforces error-budget policies.
- Product launch gating: service must have >= 30 days of SLO history and > 25% remaining error budget to proceed with high-risk experiments; otherwise a risk waiver must be recorded.

Appendix: Quick commands and PromQL snippets
-------------------------------------------
- Error rate (PromQL):
  sum(rate(request_total{job="service"} - request_success_total{job="service"}[5m])) / sum(rate(request_total{job="service"}[5m]))
- SLO burn rate (simplified):
  (1 - request_success_ratio_30d) / error_budget_per_30d
- Scale CLI examples:
  - redwoodctl scale --pool api-inference-us-west-2 --replicas 6
  - redwoodctl rollback --service inference-api --to-tag v2026-07-12
